```elisp
      (lambda ()
        (let ((task (react-async
                      (let ((response (react-await (react-fetch-async
                                                    (format "/notes/%s" (react-props self :id))))))
                        (react-set-state self :text (plist-get response :text))))))
          (lambda () (react-task-cancel task)))))
    (or (react-state self :text) "…")))
(react-testing-render (jsx (Note (:id 1))))
(react-unmount "#app")
(react-testing-flush)
react-testing-requests
;; => nil
```

## Testing

`lisp/react-testing.el` is a page made of Lisp data, for ERT. It applies the operations `react-flush` returns, as the host would, and keeps the tree, the attributes, the properties, the listeners (with their `react-handler` options), and what Lisp asked of the page. A test renders, finds elements, clicks and types, answers requests, and looks. It runs in any Emacs; the page's own Emacs 30.2 runs it under Node with wasmacs's `tools/scripts/ert.mjs`.

```sh
emacs --batch -Q -L path/to/elisp-react/lisp -L . -l app-test.el -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit
```

`-L .` puts the application's directory on `load-path`: `react-testing-load` and `load` find a relative file name there, not in the current directory. Node ids are the numbers Lisp chose (`:target` in events). Differences from a browser: there is no default action, no `preventDefault`, no FormData rules (see `react-testing-submit`), no layout, and `react-navigate` changes nothing (it is only recorded in `react-testing-told`).

#### react-testing-render

`(react-testing-render ELEMENT &optional SELECTOR)` → the root instance, or nil

Starts afresh (`react-testing-reset`), mounts `ELEMENT` at `SELECTOR` (default `"#app"`) and applies the operations. Returns the root component instance when `ELEMENT` is a component.

#### react-testing-load

`(react-testing-load FILE)` → nil

Starts afresh and loads `FILE`, an application that mounts itself, then applies the operations. `FILE` is found as `load` finds it.

#### react-testing-reset

`(react-testing-reset)` → nil

Forgets everything on both sides (`react-reset` and the fake page). The address becomes `http://localhost/` (`:pathname "/"`), the locale `(:languages ["en"] :timeZone "UTC" :offset 0)`.

#### react-testing-flush

`(react-testing-flush)` → nil

Applies what Lisp has pending (`react-flush`) to the fake page. Needed after `react-mount`, `load` or a direct `react-set-state`; the other `react-testing-` functions that act apply their own operations.

#### react-testing-storage

`(react-testing-storage KEY VALUE)` → nil

Makes the page's storage hold `VALUE` under `KEY`, as if an earlier visit had stored it. `react-testing-render` and `react-testing-load` reset the storage, so the order is `react-testing-reset`, `react-testing-storage`, then `react-mount` or `load`, then `react-testing-flush`.

#### react-testing-location

`(react-testing-location HREF)` → nil

Makes `HREF` the address and tells Lisp (the location watchers run), then applies the operations. `:search` and `:hash` are taken from `HREF`; `:pathname` is always `"/"`.

#### react-testing-find-all

`(react-testing-find-all &key TAG CLASS TEXT ATTRIBUTE SELECTOR)` → a list of node ids

The elements that match every given criterion, in document order: `TAG` (a symbol or string), `CLASS` (one of its classes), `TEXT` (its whole text, children included), `ATTRIBUTE` (`(NAME VALUE)`, both strings). `SELECTOR` limits the search to one root.

#### react-testing-find

`(react-testing-find &key TAG CLASS TEXT ATTRIBUTE SELECTOR)` → a node id

The first element that matches; signals `react-testing: no element matches ...` when there is none.

#### react-testing-text

`(react-testing-text ID)` → a string

The text of the node `ID` and everything in it. For an element with `:inner-html`, the HTML as given.

#### react-testing-attribute

`(react-testing-attribute ID NAME)` → a string, or nil

The attribute `NAME` (a string) of the node `ID`: `""` for one set with `t`, nil when absent.

#### react-testing-property

`(react-testing-property ID NAME)` → the value

The DOM property `NAME` (`"value"`, `"checked"`, or one of `react-set-property`) that Lisp set on the node `ID`, or that `react-testing-input` typed. `"checked"` is `t` or nil.

#### react-testing-html

`(react-testing-html &optional SELECTOR)` → a string, or nil

The fake page at `SELECTOR` (default `"#app"`) as HTML, for a quick look: text is not escaped, every element has an end tag, attributes come in the order they were last set.

#### react-testing-dispatch

`(react-testing-dispatch ID NAME &optional EVENT)` → nil

The event `NAME` happens on the node `ID` with the plist `EVENT` (`:type NAME :target ID` are added). It goes up through the node and its parents, running each listener of that name, as in a browser, honouring the `react-handler` options `:self`, `:keys` and `:stop`. Use it for events without a helper: `(react-testing-dispatch id "change" '(:checked t))`.

#### react-testing-click

`(react-testing-click ID)` → nil

A `click` event with no other data.

#### react-testing-input

`(react-testing-input ID VALUE)` → nil

Types `VALUE` into the input `ID`: sets its `value` property, then an `input` event and a `change` event with `:value VALUE`.

#### react-testing-key

`(react-testing-key ID KEY)` → nil

A `keydown` event with `:key KEY` (`"Enter"`, `"a"`).

#### react-testing-submit

`(react-testing-submit ID)` → nil

A `submit` event on the form `ID`, with `:form` built from every element in it that has a `name` attribute: its `value` property, else its `value` attribute, else `""`. Unlike a browser it includes unchecked checkboxes and every named button.

#### react-testing-answer

`(react-testing-answer COMMAND VALUE &optional OK)` → the request's argument

Answers the oldest waiting request of `COMMAND` (`"fetch"`, `"timeout"`, `"page-listen"`, a page command) with `VALUE`, successfully unless `OK` is `:fail`, and applies the operations. Signals `react-testing: nothing waits for COMMAND` when there is none. The request leaves `react-testing-requests` at this answer, also a kept one (a page listener, a media query, a connection): the test kit answers it once. Intervals are fired again and again by `react-testing-time-passes`.

#### react-testing-answer-fetch

`(react-testing-answer-fetch STATUS TEXT)` → the fetch's argument, `(:url ... :method ...)`

Answers the oldest waiting fetch with the response `(:status STATUS :ok (< STATUS 400) :text TEXT :headers nil)`.

#### react-testing-time-passes

`(react-testing-time-passes)` → nil

Fires every timeout that is waiting now, once (and forgets it), and every interval once. Timers started by what fires wait for the next call.

#### react-testing-requests

A variable: what Lisp asked of the page and waits for, oldest first, each `(REQUEST COMMAND ARGUMENT)`. Cancelled requests are taken out.

#### react-testing-told

A variable: what Lisp told the page, oldest first, each `(COMMAND ARGUMENT)`: `("storage-set" (:key ... :value ...))`, `("navigate" (:url ... :replace ...))`, `("title" (:text ...))`.

#### react-testing-invoked

A variable: methods called on nodes, oldest first, each `(ID METHOD ARGS...)`.

## Rules and pitfalls

1. Start every file with `;;; NAME.el --- ...  -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-`. The page adds the cookie when the first line lacks it, but a native Emacs (tests, a server) loads such a file with dynamic binding, and closures over `self` fail with `void-variable`.
2. A native Emacs needs `react.el` loaded before it compiles an application file: put `(require 'react)` at the top, or `-l react` on the command line. Otherwise `jsx` and `react-async` compile as function calls. As a lint, byte-compile with warnings as errors: `emacs --batch -Q -L path/to/lisp -l react --eval '(setq byte-compile-error-on-warn t)' -f batch-byte-compile app.el`.
3. `react-mount` renders at once. Every component it uses must be defined by then: put `react-mount` last, in the last file. A component defined in a later file renders as an unknown element (with a message) and stays one.
4. List library files before the files that `require` them, and end them with `(provide 'NAME)`. A file required before its turn is loaded twice (from source by `require`, compiled in its turn), so its top-level forms run twice.
5. In `jsx`, components are Capitalized names. A lowercase component name works only in the plain list form; in `jsx` it is a function call.
6. A component named like an HTML or SVG tag (`label`, `button`, `title`) replaces that tag in every element of the page.
7. Inside `jsx`, a list that starts with a tag name is markup. A function named like a tag (`mark`, or your own `label`, `filter`, `search`, `time`, `data`) cannot be called there directly; compute the value before, or use `funcall`.
8. All files share one Emacs. Prefix global function and variable names with the application's name; a `defun` of an existing name replaces it for everything, `react.el` included.
9. Give every child of a list that changes a `:key`, unique among its siblings. Without keys children are matched by position, and the state of row components stays with the position, not the row.
10. Never modify state in place (`setcar`, `plist-put` on a plist in state, `nconc`, `delete`, `sort` on the state's list). Build new values: `react-plist-with`, `mapcar`, `seq-remove`, `append`. `:pure`, `:should-update`, `react-changed-p` and context compare lists by identity.
11. In a handler, read state when the event happens, `(react-state self :todos)`, not a value the render captured: two quick events would otherwise both start from the old value. After a `react-await`, read state again.
12. The event name is the DOM event type after `:on-`: `:on-keydown`, `:on-dblclick`, `:on-pointerdown`. `:on-key-down` listens for an event `key-down` that never comes.
13. Lisp cannot prevent a default action after the fact. Declare it: `(react-handler f :prevent t)`. A form's `submit` is always prevented; a `<button>` in a form submits it unless it has `:type "button"`.
14. Symbols, keywords and vectors are not children (`Not an element`). Write `(symbol-name x)` or `(format "%s" x)`; turn a vector from `react-response-json` into a list with `(append v nil)` or `mapcar`.
15. `:value` makes an input controlled: set state from `:on-input`, or the next render writes the old value back.
16. `react-location`, `react-locale` and `react-storage-get` are not state. A component that reads them does not render again when they change: watch them (`react-location-watch`, `react-storage-watch`) and set state or `react-force-update`.
17. What starts in `:did-mount` or an effect stops in `:will-unmount` or the effect's cleanup: `react-set-interval`, `react-listen-page`, `react-media-query`, `react-observe-visible`, `react-websocket`, `react-event-source`, `react-location-watch`, `react-storage-watch`. Otherwise they go on calling a component that is gone.
18. Do not call `react-set-state` unconditionally in `:render` or `:did-update`: the flush gives up after 100 rounds with `"Components keep changing state while rendering"`.
19. `react-effect` keys are symbols, unique within the component; deps are compared with `equal`; deps nil runs once.
20. `react-await` only where generator.el can rewrite it: not inside `lambda`, `mapcar`, `seq-map`, `cl-loop`, `with-temp-buffer`, `save-excursion` or `unwind-protect`. Loop with `dolist`, `dotimes` or `while`.
21. A call from the host cannot be interrupted. Past the timeout (30 s) Emacs is stopped for good. Break long work inside `react-async` with `(react-await (react-sleep 0))`.
22. Everything sent to the page is JSON: arguments of `react-host-call`, `react-host-tell` and `react-invoke`, `:headers`. Use plists with keyword keys, vectors, strings, numbers, `t`, `:false` and nil. A symbol or a plain list (`'("a" "b")`) has no JSON form and makes the whole answer of that call fail; use `vconcat` for arrays and `symbol-name` for symbols.
23. Use only the `react-invoke` methods and `react-set-property` properties listed, and only commands the host or the page defines. An unknown method or command makes the host drop the rest of that answer's operations.
24. `react-query`'s loader returns a function of `(RESOLVE REJECT)`, such as `(react-fetch-async URL)`; a `react-async` task there is an error in the render.
25. `:ref` on a component element is just a prop. To reach an element a child renders, pass `(react-make-ref self NAME)` down under a prop of your own and put it on the element.
26. A string with raw bytes (`json-serialize` output, `url-unhex-string`) is decoded as UTF-8; what is still not text becomes U+FFFD, with a message. Fetch bytes with `:as 'base64`.
27. Reloading a file (the host's `load`) keeps `defvar` values and re-runs `defconst`, `setq` and `defun`. Redefined components keep their state; a changed `:initial-state` shows only on a new instance or after a page reload.
28. In tests, `react-testing-render` and `react-testing-load` reset the storage and the address: set them with `react-testing-storage` after `react-testing-reset`, then mount or `load`, then `react-testing-flush`.
29. Do not `require` `react-testing` in the page: it is not on the page's `load-path`. Keep tests in files the page does not list.
30. Keep secrets out of `localStorage`: every page of an origin can read it, and the compiled code kept there too.

## Worked examples

Each example is a file and a test. Run a test with the command in [Testing](#testing).

### Counter

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Counter</title></head>
  <body>
    <div id="app">Loading Emacs…</div>
    <script type="text/emacs-lisp" src="counter.el"></script>
    <script type="module" src="https://modeverv.github.io/elisp-react/js/elisp-react.js"></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

```elisp
;;; counter.el --- a counter  -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-

(require 'react)

(react-define-component 'Counter
  :initial-state (lambda (props) (list :count (or (plist-get props :start) 0)))
  :render
  (lambda (self)
    (let ((count (react-state self :count)))
      (jsx (div (:class "counter")
             (p (:class "count") (format "Count: %d" count))
             (button (:class "increment"
                      :on-click (lambda (_event)
                                  (react-set-state self :count (1+ (react-state self :count)))))
               "+1")
             (button (:class "reset" :disabled (= count 0)
                      :on-click (lambda (_event) (react-set-state self :count 0)))
               "reset"))))))

(react-mount (jsx (Counter (:start 3))) "#app")
```

```elisp
;;; counter-test.el --- tests of counter.el  -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-

(require 'ert)
(require 'react-testing)

(ert-deftest counter-counts-and-resets ()
  (react-testing-load "counter.el")
  (should (equal (react-testing-text (react-testing-find :class "count")) "Count: 3"))
  (react-testing-click (react-testing-find :class "increment"))
  (should (equal (react-testing-text (react-testing-find :class "count")) "Count: 4"))
  (should-not (react-testing-attribute (react-testing-find :class "reset") "disabled"))
  (react-testing-click (react-testing-find :class "reset"))
  (should (equal (react-testing-text (react-testing-find :class "count")) "Count: 0"))
  (should (equal (react-testing-attribute (react-testing-find :class "reset") "disabled") "")))
```

### Todo list

A keyed list, a controlled input, a form submit, rows that skip their render, and the list kept in `localStorage`.

```elisp
;;; todos.el --- a todo list  -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-

(require 'react)
(require 'seq)
(require 'subr-x)

(defun todos-next-id (todos)
  (1+ (apply #'max 0 (mapcar (lambda (todo) (plist-get todo :id)) todos))))

(react-define-component 'TodoItem
  ;; Renders only when its todo changed; the handlers read the function
  ;; props when the event happens.
  :pure t
  :render
  (lambda (self)
    (let ((todo (react-props self :todo)))
      (jsx (li (:class (if (plist-get todo :done) "todo done" "todo"))
             (input (:type "checkbox" :class "toggle" :checked (plist-get todo :done)
                     :on-change (lambda (_event)
                                  (funcall (react-props self :on-toggle) (plist-get todo :id)))))
             (span (:class "text") (plist-get todo :text))
             (button (:type "button" :class "delete"
                      :on-click (lambda (_event)
                                  (funcall (react-props self :on-delete) (plist-get todo :id))))
               "×"))))))

(react-define-component 'TodoApp
  :initial-state (lambda (_props) (list :todos (react-storage-get "todos" nil) :draft ""))
  :did-update (lambda (self _previous-props previous-state)
                (unless (eq (react-state self :todos) (plist-get previous-state :todos))
                  (react-storage-set "todos" (react-state self :todos))))
  :render
  (lambda (self)
    (let* ((todos (react-state self :todos))
           (toggle-todo
            (lambda (id)
              (react-set-state
               self :todos
               (mapcar (lambda (todo)
                         (if (= (plist-get todo :id) id)
                             (react-plist-with todo :done (not (plist-get todo :done)))
                           todo))
                       (react-state self :todos)))))
           (delete-todo
            (lambda (id)
              (react-set-state
               self :todos
               (seq-remove (lambda (todo) (= (plist-get todo :id) id)) (react-state self :todos)))))
           (add-todo
            (lambda (event)
              (let ((text (string-trim (or (react-form-value event "text") "")))
                    (todos (react-state self :todos)))
                (unless (string-empty-p text)
                  (react-set-state
                   self
                   :todos (append todos (list (list :id (todos-next-id todos) :text text :done nil)))
                   :draft ""))))))
      (jsx (main
             (form (:class "new" :on-submit add-todo)
               (input (:name "text" :class "new-text" :placeholder "What needs to be done?"
                       :value (react-state self :draft)
                       :on-input (lambda (event) (react-set-state self :draft (plist-get event :value)))))
               (button (:class "add" :disabled (string-empty-p (string-trim (react-state self :draft))))
                 "add"))
             (ul (:class "todos")
               (mapcar (lambda (todo)
                         (jsx (TodoItem (:key (plist-get todo :id) :todo todo
                                         :on-toggle toggle-todo :on-delete delete-todo))))
                       todos))
             (p (:class "left")
               (format "%d left" (seq-count (lambda (todo) (not (plist-get todo :done))) todos))))))))

(react-mount (jsx (TodoApp)) "#app")
```

### Loading data

`react-async` with a loading state, an error state and a retry. `quotes.json` is an array of `{"id": ..., "text": ...}`.

```elisp
;;; quotes.el --- loading data with react-async  -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-

(require 'react)

(defun quotes-load (self)
  "Load the quotes into SELF's state: loading, then loaded or failed."
  (react-async
    (react-set-state self :status 'loading :error nil)
    (condition-case failure
        (let ((response (react-await (react-fetch-async "quotes.json"))))
          (if (plist-get response :ok)
              (react-set-state self :status 'loaded
                               :quotes (append (react-response-json response) nil))
            (react-set-state self :status 'failed
                             :error (format "HTTP %d" (plist-get response :status)))))
      ;; No response at all: offline, refused.
      (react-async-error (react-set-state self :status 'failed :error (cadr failure))))))

(react-define-component 'Quotes
  :initial-state (lambda (_props) (list :status 'loading :quotes nil :error nil))
  :did-mount (lambda (self) (quotes-load self))
  :render
  (lambda (self)
    (pcase (react-state self :status)
      ('loading (jsx (p (:class "status") "Loading…")))
      ('failed (jsx (div (p (:class "error") (react-state self :error))
                         (button (:class "retry" :on-click (lambda (_event) (quotes-load self)))
                           "retry"))))
      (_ (jsx (ul (:class "quotes")
                (mapcar (lambda (item) (jsx (li (:key (plist-get item :id)) (plist-get item :text))))
                        (react-state self :quotes))))))))

(react-mount (jsx (Quotes)) "#app")
```

```elisp
;;; quotes-test.el --- tests of quotes.el  -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-

(require 'ert)
(require 'react-testing)

(ert-deftest quotes-load-fail-retry ()
  (react-testing-load "quotes.el")
  (should (equal (react-testing-text (react-testing-find :class "status")) "Loading…"))
  ;; No response at all.
  (should (equal (plist-get (react-testing-answer "fetch" "Failed to fetch" :fail) :url) "quotes.json"))
  (should (equal (react-testing-text (react-testing-find :class "error")) "Failed to fetch"))
  ;; Retry: an HTTP error, then data.
  (react-testing-click (react-testing-find :class "retry"))
  (react-testing-answer-fetch 500 "")
  (should (equal (react-testing-text (react-testing-find :class "error")) "HTTP 500"))
  (react-testing-click (react-testing-find :class "retry"))
  (react-testing-answer-fetch 200 "[{\"id\":1,\"text\":\"Simple things should be simple.\"}]")
  (should (equal (mapcar #'react-testing-text (react-testing-find-all :tag 'li))
                 '("Simple things should be simple."))))
```

### Theme from a context

A theme provided at the top, read two levels below, through a `:pure` component that skips its render.

```elisp
;;; theme.el --- context  -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-

(require 'react)

(react-define-component 'ThemedButton
  :render
  (lambda (self)
    (jsx (button (:class (list "button" (react-context self 'theme "light")))
           (react-props self :label)))))

(react-define-component 'Toolbar
  :pure t
  :render (lambda (_self) (jsx (nav (ThemedButton (:label "Save")) (ThemedButton (:label "Load"))))))

(react-define-component 'ThemeApp
  :initial-state (lambda (_props) (list :theme "light"))
  :render
  (lambda (self)
    (jsx (div
           (button (:class "switch"
                    :on-click (lambda (_event)
                                (react-set-state self :theme (if (equal (react-state self :theme) "light")
                                                                 "dark"
                                                               "light"))))
             "switch theme")
           (react-provide 'theme (react-state self :theme) (jsx (Toolbar)))))))

(react-mount (jsx (ThemeApp)) "#app")
```

```elisp
;;; theme-test.el --- tests of theme.el  -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-

(require 'ert)
(require 'react-testing)

(ert-deftest theme-reaches-buttons-below-a-pure-component ()
  (react-testing-load "theme.el")
  (should (equal (length (react-testing-find-all :class "light")) 2))
  (react-testing-click (react-testing-find :class "switch"))
  (should (equal (length (react-testing-find-all :class "dark")) 2))
  (should (equal (react-testing-attribute (react-testing-find :text "Save") "class") "button dark")))
```

### A test with react-testing.el

The todo list above, tested: stored data at the start, typing and submitting, keys keeping DOM nodes, a checkbox, and what the page was told to store.

```elisp
;;; todos-test.el --- tests of todos.el  -*- lexical-binding: t; -*-

(require 'ert)
(require 'react-testing)

(defun todos-test-texts ()
  (mapcar #'react-testing-text (react-testing-find-all :class "text")))

(ert-deftest todos-add-delete-toggle ()
  ;; Not react-testing-load: it would reset the storage set here.
  (react-testing-reset)
  (react-testing-storage "todos" '((:id 1 :text "Write tests" :done nil)))
  (load "todos.el" nil t)
  (react-testing-flush)
  (should (equal (todos-test-texts) '("Write tests")))
  (should (react-testing-attribute (react-testing-find :class "add") "disabled"))
  ;; Type, then submit the form.
  (react-testing-input (react-testing-find :class "new-text") "Run them")
  (should-not (react-testing-attribute (react-testing-find :class "add") "disabled"))
  (react-testing-submit (react-testing-find :tag 'form :class "new"))
  (should (equal (todos-test-texts) '("Write tests" "Run them")))
  (should (equal (react-testing-property (react-testing-find :class "new-text") "value") ""))
  ;; Keys: the second row keeps its DOM node when the first goes.
  (let ((second-row (cadr (react-testing-find-all :tag 'li))))
    (react-testing-click (car (react-testing-find-all :class "delete")))
    (should (equal (react-testing-find-all :tag 'li) (list second-row))))
  ;; A checkbox: a change event.
  (react-testing-dispatch (react-testing-find :class "toggle") "change" '(:checked t))
  (should (equal (react-testing-text (react-testing-find :class "left")) "0 left"))
  (should (equal (react-testing-attribute (react-testing-find :tag 'li) "class") "todo done"))
  ;; The page was told to store the list.
  (let ((stored (car (last react-testing-told))))
    (should (equal (car stored) "storage-set"))
    (should (equal (read (plist-get (cadr stored) :value))
                   '((:id 2 :text "Run them" :done t))))))
```
